column1: # What a comparison returns. Registering this kind is what turns
# `true` and `false` are not translated, and that is this file's finding
# rather than an oversight it hides: the kind ships no vocabulary at all,
# so `formatValue` degrades to the unit key in every language. A Korean
# engine answering "true" is what the code does today, and a row asserting
# it is what makes a later `boolean/locale/ko` a visible diff here.
# No space between a number and its unit, on either side of a comparison.
# The particles, glued to the unit and stripped off it. On a bare quantity
# the glue is harmless; a conversion needs the Latin alias underneath,
# because a particle stuck to a Hangul unit does not separate from it.
# Sino-Korean numerals, counted in ten-thousands: 만 is one word for 10000.
# No number agreement anywhere. One unit word serves every count.
